page: Amazon Web Services c6a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25 percent. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average read performance, but write performance for large, uncached blocks is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25 percent. The instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds for small language models, while prompt processing and larger model inference remain average.

The c6a.4xlarge provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a cost-efficiency perspective, its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer a balanced compute-heavy profile without the overhead of bundled local storage. This makes it a viable option for compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, web serving, text processing, and moderate database operations.
